memory_candidates.content: When adding a new value to a discriminator enum that downstream shell consumers branch on, audit every consumer for a CLOSED `case`/`if` with no default arm. In agent-system/extensions/core, orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's `defer_reason` is consumed by orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh via `case "$dr" in` with arms for only the three known values and NO `*)` arm: an unrecognized value leaves the task excluded from dispatch (decision stays "defer") but writes no defer_ledger entry and emits no warning -- silent exclusion, worse than mis-bucketing. By contrast a `select()`-based jq consumer (orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh's classes) is inert but safe against an unknown value. The general rule: `select()`-style positive-match consumers degrade to invisible-but-harmless; closed switch consumers degrade to invisible-and-harmful. Add the loud default arm in the same change set that introduces the new enum value, and record which consumer class each site belongs to.
